items.title: The genuine Hessian integral represents the full gradient difference

source.anchor: Lemma4.6 proof, actual H(x,xprime) and inherited curvature, HTML568-572
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang; scoped actual Hessian secant constructor, with explicit shared Hilbert/signed generalization.

items.statement: For every complete real inner-product space E, every globally C2 real f with signed global genuine-Hessian diagonal bounds alpha,beta, and all x,y, let phi(t) be the Riesz operator of D2f(y+t(x-y)) and H=integral_0^1 phi(t) dt in ordinary Lebesgue measure. Then phi is interval integrable, gradient f x-gradient f y=H(x-y), H is symmetric, all v satisfy alpha||v||^2<=inner(Hv,v)<=beta||v||^2, and ||H||op<=max(|alpha|,|beta|). In finite Euclidean space this specializes to the source actual H with alpha=1/(2kappa),beta=1; V_eta smoothness/curvature must still be proved separately.
assumptions: E is a complete real inner-product space (a real Hilbert space), including dimension zero. f:E->R is globally C2 in the Frechet sense. x,y and every test vector range over all E.
alpha,beta are real and may be signed. For every z,v, alpha||v||^2 <= D2f(z)[v,v] <= beta||v||^2. These are bounds on the genuine nested Frechet derivative, not on an independently supplied operator.

H(x,y) is the ordinary Lebesgue Bochner integral on[0,1] of the Riesz-represented D2f(y+t(x-y)). Its symmetry, continuity/measurability/integrability and secant identity are conclusions derived from C2, not hypotheses. Completeness permits the Riesz identification and Bochner operator integral.

formulae.label: Actual Hessian secant operator
formulae.tex: H(x,y)=\int_0^1[D^2f(y+t(x-y))]^{\sharp}\,dt,\quad\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)=H(x,y)(x-y),\quad\alpha I\preceq H\preceq\beta I,\quad\|H\|_{\rm op}\le\max(|\alpha|,|\beta|).

obligations.label: Actual Hessian integral: gradient difference, symmetry, bounds and norm
Smoothed potential, actual averaged H/expansion and both main/composition (remaining)

bindings.boundary: Only the actual Hessian-segment constructor in Lemma4.6. The source smoothed-potential C2/curvature producer, actual Picard-node weighted average H, first-order endpoint expansion/operator remainder, deterministic K contraction, stochastic Khat/Kbar, repeated history, PBPS and both full main results/composition remain independent. The signed Hilbert generalization is background, not an extra assumption on the finite-dimensional source theorem. No probability/cost guarantee or implemented kernel is asserted here.
